sections.h2: How do I search Leon County, Texas property records?
sections.html:
Leon County's deed and official records are online, and the County Clerk's office in Centerville also has eight public search stations where you can look things up yourself. Staff will show you how the indexes work, but anyone is welcome to do their own research.

Deed and official records1828 forward

PlatsAvailable on the stations

The office occupies the first floor at 155 North Cass Street, Centerville, TX 75833. The clerk's page spells out a few house rules for visitors:

  • No photographs of the large Tobin maps or of images on the public stations, and no flash photography.
  • Carrying a document, page or volume out of the office is a state jail felony (Penal Code 32.47).
  • Staff give no legal advice, do not decide who owns surface or mineral rights, and do not run lien searches.
  • Attorney General Opinion WW-607 is cited for the point that the clerk has no duty to search the records and vouch for them.

sections.h2: What are the Leon County Clerk's hours and recording fee?
sections.html:
Doors are open weekdays from 7:45 a.m. until 4:45 p.m., with no break at lunch, but the recording desk shuts at 4 p.m. Whatever arrives after that goes onto the next business day's work. Payment can be cash, check or a major credit card.

The posted charge is $15 for page one of an instrument and $4 for each page after it, under a schedule the office says began on January 1, 2024. Electronic filing into the official records runs through three named vendors, Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Because schedules change, ask the clerk to confirm the amount before you send payment.

Different deputies take different work. General recording, indexing and copy requests sit with the chief deputy, while probate, civil filings, marriage licenses and vital records each have their own staff member and phone menu option.

sections.h2: What does Texas require before a Leon County deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
A land conveyance may be recorded only after the owner signs it and swears to it or acknowledges it, either before two witnesses or before an officer such as a notary, county clerk, district clerk or county court judge (Property Code 12.001(b)).

The 2023 county clerk manual describes the instruments that land in deed records: general and special warranty deeds, quitclaims, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds and tax deeds, plus lien releases, affidavits and contracts of sale. Its statutory base is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with other clerk charges added, and a missing grantee mailing address may add $25. For an actual filing, use the figure Leon County posts.

A recorded deed cannot be edited to add heirs later. After an owner's death, the manual points to an executor's or administrator's deed for an administered estate, a court order with the will for a muniment of title, or an affidavit of heirship when nothing else is available.

sections.h2: What is Leon County like for a homeowner or seller?
sections.html:
Leon County is rural, east of Waco on Interstate 45 between Dallas and Houston. Census Bureau data puts the mid-2025 population at 16,894, which is 7.2 percent above the April 2020 base. The county has 9,255 housing units, 6,741 households and 1,073.16 square miles of land.

For 2020 to 2024, owners occupy 76.6 percent of homes, and the typical owned home is valued at $186,400. Median monthly owner costs are $1,557 with a mortgage and $502 without, and median gross rent is $907. Workers travel 29.3 minutes on average to a job. More than a quarter of the population, 27.9 percent, is 65 or older.

According to the Handbook of Texas, the county was carved from Robertson County in 1846. Leona served first as seat of government, and Centerville took over in 1851. Buffalo is the biggest community, and Jewett, Normangee, Oakwood and Marquez are also named. U.S. 79 crosses east to west, the Trinity River marks the eastern edge, and Lake Limestone fills part of the northwest corner. Oil and gas, agribusiness and lumber anchor the economy.

sections.h2: Who handles Leon County values and tax bills?
sections.html:
The Leon Central Appraisal District sets values and the county tax assessor-collector issues bills. The county's page directs owners with account changes or value questions to the appraisal district at 141 W. St. Mary's, Centerville, TX 75833, telephone 903-536-2252.

That page also names the firms that chase delinquent accounts for each unit. One Waco firm covers the county, a Corsicana firm covers Normangee ISD, and a Tyler firm covers Buffalo ISD, the City of Marquez and Oakwood ISD. If a collection letter shows up, the unit that sent it tells you which firm to contact.

Across Texas, values are fixed on January 1, bills arrive in October and January 31 is the final day to pay penalty-free. Because each year's tax lien attaches on January 1, a Leon County house carries that year's tax into any sale. Our Leon County property tax guide covers the tax office itself.

sections.h2: What title problems turn up in the Leon County records?
sections.html:
The commonest one is an estate nobody opened. With more than a quarter of residents past 65, a parent's name often remains the last owner on the deed, and the file needs a legal path to the heirs.

  • A will is generally probated within four years of death, though a court may take a late filing for an acceptable reason.
  • A small estate affidavit needs no will, no pending administration, assets of $75,000 or less outside homestead and exempt property, and every heir's agreement. Two disinterested witnesses swear to it, and the death must be at least 30 days old.
  • A muniment of title lets a will serve as proof of ownership when the only debts are real estate liens.
  • An affidavit of heirship is filed with the Leon County Clerk, but no rule makes a buyer or lender rely on it.

Heirs who want a homestead exemption and are not named on a recorded deed must give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the owner's death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Leon County house with a title or lien problem?
sections.html: Yes. A buyer paying cash can purchase the property as it stands, and the closing agent clears recorded items where payoffs can be documented. If you found an unreleased mortgage, a probate gap or a back tax bill in the Leon County records, send us the details and we will outline the likely route to closing.

faqs.q: What time does the Leon County Clerk stop recording documents?
faqs.a: At 4 p.m., although the office stays open until 4:45 p.m. on weekdays. Papers that arrive later are handled the following business day.

faqs.q: How much does the Leon County Clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The clerk's page lists $15 for page one and $4 for every added page of an instrument, effective January 1, 2024. Ask the office to confirm the amount when you file.

faqs.q: Are Leon County deed records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk says deed and official records are online, and the same records back to 1828 can be viewed on public stations in the Centerville office.

faqs.q: Will the Leon County Clerk tell me who owns the minerals?
faqs.a: No. The clerk's page says staff cannot determine surface or mineral ownership or run lien searches, so that work falls to a title company or attorney.

faqs.q: Where do I contest a Leon County appraisal?
faqs.a: Call the Leon Central Appraisal District at 903-536-2252. A protest to the appraisal review board is due May 15 or by the 30th day after the notice of value is delivered, whichever falls later.
